question: Which Primary Health Care principle ensures that health services are within easy reach of everyone?
explanation: Accessibility is the core principle that guarantees health services are physically and socially within reach of every community member without discrimination. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T3#BMP117_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why might a pregnant woman choose to pass a nearby clinic and travel further to another one?

options.A: Distant facilities always offer free medications regardless of type
options.B: She may feel the distant facility is more welcoming or affordable
options.C: Primary health care guidelines strictly require traveling past the first facility
options.D: Government policy bans women from using their closest health post

explanation: Accessibility includes how acceptable and affordable a clinic feels. Clients will travel further if local services lack a welcoming environment or fair pricing. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T3#BMP117_U1_T3_h1)

question: What type of barrier is caused by poor roads and long distances when trying to reach a clinic?
explanation: Geographical accessibility refers to physical distance, difficult terrain, and transportation challenges that affect getting to a health facility. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T3#BMP117_U1_T3_h2)

question: A pregnant woman in labor delays coming to the clinic because she has no money for transport or drugs. Which barrier is this?
explanation: When a client cannot afford transport or medical items, financial barriers are preventing them from receiving timely care. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T3#BMP117_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the main goal of health equity when distributing resources?

options.A: Providing free care only to political leaders
options.B: Allocating resources based on actual health needs
options.C: Building identical clinics in every single village
options.D: Focusing all funds on high-paying urban populations

explanation: Equity means distributing resources fairly based on where the greatest health needs are, rather than based on wealth or social status. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T3#BMP117_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why do healthcare resources often fail to reach rural populations equitably?

options.A: Facilities tend to cluster in wealthy urban centers
options.B: Primary health care laws prohibit building clinics outside cities
options.C: Rural communities explicitly ban government health clinics
options.D: Rural residents never experience medical complications

explanation: An urban focus in infrastructure development frequently leaves remote and rural populations underserved and lacking proper facilities. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T3#BMP117_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which social factor frequently delays a woman from seeking timely maternity care?

options.A: Excessive availability of modern laboratory equipment
options.B: Mandatory attendance at antenatal health talks
options.C: Husbands holding the final authority on family health decisions
options.D: Strict government laws against traditional naming ceremonies

explanation: In many households, decision-making structures where male heads hold the primary authority can cause delays in accessing emergency care. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T3#BMP117_U1_T3_h4)

question: How should a midwife best respond when a community relies heavily on traditional birth attendants?

options.A: Report all community elders to the police immediately
options.B: Forbid pregnant women from speaking to traditional healers
options.C: Ignore the community and close the local health post
options.D: Engage respectfully and build referral linkages with them

explanation: Collaborative engagement and respectful communication with traditional birth attendants achieve much better maternal outcomes than confrontation. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T3#BMP117_U1_T3_h4)

question: What strategy involves training community health workers to provide specific clinical services when skilled staff are scarce?
explanation: Task shifting allows qualified community health workers to safely handle designated clinical duties to help expand the reach of healthcare services. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T3#BMP117_U1_T3_h5)

question: How do mobile health clinics improve maternal and child health access in remote settlements?

options.A: By offering free luxury transport to private city hospitals
options.B: By replacing all permanent primary health care centers with buses
options.C: By bringing essential clinical services directly to hard-to-reach settlements
options.D: By forcing rural residents to migrate permanently to urban centers

explanation: Mobile clinics solve geographical barriers by traveling directly to populations that do not have a static health facility nearby. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T3#BMP117_U1_T3_h5)
